text:
Running a production database on a 2 GB VPS sounds like a bad idea. It mostly is, but it also taught us more about Postgres than anything else we've done.

We started out optimistic and set `shared_buffers` to 512 MB, since a bigger cache seemed like an obvious win. It wasn't. We got three OOM kills in the first month. The Linux kernel won't negotiate, and a memory budget has to cover every connection, every worker and every background process, not just the cache.

What actually fixed things was PgBouncer. Pooling connections took us from 200 active connections down to 20. Memory pressure eased, latency went down, and the little VPS started handling far more load than its specs suggest.

This post covers what we learned, what we got wrong, and the tuning changes that got the setup from unstable to dependable.
